chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Why the interview names so many sidemen
summary: Hinton explains the oral history aims to credit the many musicians who made the great bands great.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Butter, you and I and these very long lucrative years that we've had in jazz have had such a great opportunity to meet so many musicians --
-- and we would like to talk about them and mention them --

-- for posterity so people will know that there wasn't just a handful that won the awards but that a great number of musicians contributed to these bands to make them as great as they were. And I think this is one of the main things -- object in doing this kind of an oral history is to let the people know, the students of jazz and lovers of jazz know the great people that comprise the making up of these great bands. So I know, between you and I
we'll probably miss some which we really don't intend to miss but it's going to be hard because your memory is so beautiful. But I'd like to --
Of course, something's always coming to you, you know, that you can say. --
And so we keep rehashing things about different ones.
